name: Identity Fusion NG
description: Identity Fusion NG is a connector that allows you to manage Identity Fusion accounts by mapping account attributes from multiple sources, defining new attributes and unique identifiers, and matching accounts with existing identities to prevent duplicates.

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Configure how this connector connects to Identity Security Cloud.

Use Identity Security Cloud API URL to specify the base URL of your ISC tenant (for example, https://tenant.api.identitynow.com).

Provide the Personal Access Token ID and Personal Access Token Secret for an account that has the required API permissions (Sources, Identities, Accounts, Workflows/Forms). These values are used to authenticate all connector operations.

items.label: Identity Security Cloud API URL
items.helpKey: Base URL of your Identity Security Cloud tenant (format: https://<tenant>.api.identitynow.com)

items.label: Personal Access Token ID
items.helpKey: Enter the Client ID from your Personal Access Token. The token must have permissions to manage sources, identities, accounts, and forms

items.label: Personal Access Token secret
items.helpKey: Enter the Client Secret from your Personal Access Token. This value is stored securely and should be rotated periodically

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Define which identities are in scope.

Limit processing using an Identity Scope Query (standard ISC search syntax). Toggle Include identities in the scope to establish a baseline for Match.

items.label: Include identities in the scope?
items.helpKey: When enabled, existing identities are included alongside accounts from your configured sources. Turn this on if you want to define attributes from identity data or use identities as a baseline for detecting potential matches

items.label: Identity Scope Query
items.helpKey: Filter which identities are included using a search query. Use * for all identities, or narrow results with filters like attributes.cloudLifecycleState:active or source.name:"Workday"

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Select and configure authoritative account sources.

  • Source type & behavior: Define role (Authoritative, Record, Orphan) and handling for unmatched non-identity accounts (disable, defer).
  • Aggregation & correlation: Control timing (delays, retries), optimized aggregation, and correlation strategy (in-process or reverse).
  • Filtering & limits: Process subsets via API/JMESPath filters and set batch capacities.

items.label: Source name
items.helpKey: Enter the exact name of the source as it appears in Identity Security Cloud (case-sensitive)

items.label: Enabled
items.helpKey: Turn off to temporarily exclude this source from processing without removing it

items.label: Source type
items.helpKey: Choose how accounts from this source are handled. 'Authoritative accounts' creates new Fusion accounts for unmatched entries (default). 'Records' processes accounts for Map & Define but does not create Fusion accounts for unmatched ones. 'Orphan accounts' skips unmatched accounts entirely, with an option to disable them

items.label: Disable non-matching accounts
items.helpKey: Automatically disable orphan accounts that no longer match any identity after aggregation

items.label: Deferred matching
items.helpKey: Deferred matching: after identity matching, also compare this account to other new unmatched accounts from the same source in this run. If the only strong match is one of those same-source peers, defer instead of creating another Fusion identity until a later run. Off: skip that check and use normal unmatched handling. Only peers from this source are considered; cross-source checks are never performed.

items.label: Include record accounts in Match
items.helpKey: Enable when record accounts should be matched against Fusion identities. Disable to skip Match; Map & Define and unique attributes still run.

items.label: Accounts API filter
items.helpKey: Server-side ISC account filter sent to the Accounts API (filters parameter). Use this to reduce records returned from ISC. Reference: https://developer.sailpoint.com/docs/api/v2025/list-accounts

items.label: Accounts JMESPath filter
items.helpKey: Client-side JMESPath expression applied after accounts are fetched (page-wise as { accounts: [...] }). The expression must return an array of account objects to keep. Reference: https://jmespath.org/

items.label: Aggregation batch size
items.helpKey: Limit the number of accounts processed per run. Leave empty to process all accounts. Useful when loading large datasets for the first time

items.label: Account aggregation mode
items.helpKey: Choose when to pull the latest accounts from this source. 'Aggregate before processing' refreshes accounts first. 'Delayed aggregation' refreshes after processing completes. 'Do not aggregate' uses existing account data. Note: delimited file sources do not support aggregation

items.label: Aggregation wait timeout (minutes)
items.helpKey: Maximum time to wait for this source's aggregation to finish when using Aggregate before processing. The connector checks task status every 30 seconds until completion or this timeout. Increase for very large sources.

items.label: Aggregation delay (minutes)
items.helpKey: How many minutes to wait after processing completes before refreshing accounts from this source

items.label: Optimized aggregation
items.helpKey: Only process accounts that have changed since the last run, improving performance. Disable this if you use reverse correlation, which requires all accounts to be reprocessed

items.label: Optimized aggregation
items.helpKey: Only process accounts that have changed since the last run, improving performance. Disable this if you use reverse correlation, which requires all accounts to be reprocessed

items.label: Correlation mode
items.helpKey: Choose how uncorrelated source accounts are linked to identities. 'Correlate missing accounts on aggregation' links them automatically during processing. 'Reverse correlation from managed source' creates/uses a dedicated identity attribute and correlation rule so ISC can match them. 'Do not correlate' leaves them unlinked

items.label: Correlation attribute display name
items.helpKey: Friendly display label for the reverse-correlation attribute shown in Identity Security Cloud

items.label: Correlation attribute name
items.helpKey: Internal name for the attribute used to link accounts via reverse correlation. This must be unique and cannot overlap mapped/defined attributes or existing source schema attributes

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Control account maintenance.

  • History limits: Cap the number of audit history messages stored per account.
  • Delete when empty: Remove the Fusion account if all its underlying source accounts are deleted.
  • Skip missing targets: Ignore source accounts missing a mapped native identity attribute.

items.label: Maximum history messages
items.helpKey: Number of processing history entries to keep per account. Older entries are removed automatically.

items.label: Delete accounts with no managed accounts left?
items.helpKey: Automatically remove a Fusion account when all of its linked source accounts have been deleted. Useful for cleaning up after users leave the organization

items.label: Skip accounts with missing ID?
items.helpKey: Skip accounts that are missing a unique identity value. When disabled, missing identity or display attributes are automatically populated with fallback values (UUID and account name, respectively).

items.label: Enable cascade aggregation for single account read
items.helpKey: When enabled, triggers aggregation of managed sources before fetching managed accounts during single account operations (e.g., accountRead). This ensures the most up-to-date account data is fetched before processing the fusion account. Errors during cascade aggregation are logged but do not stop the main process.

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Map and merge source attributes.

Choose a Default attribute merge mode. Then configure per-attribute rules to target specific source fields, rename them on the Fusion account, and optionally override the merge strategy or pin specific sources.

items.label: Default attribute merge from multiple sources
items.helpKey: When multiple sources provide the same attribute, choose how to combine them. 'First found' uses the value from the highest-priority source. 'Keep a list' stores all values. 'Concatenate' joins values into a single text

items.label: New attribute
items.helpKey: Name for this attribute on the Fusion account. This will appear in the account schema

items.label: Existing attributes
items.helpKey: Source attribute names to pull values from. Names must match the source account attributes exactly (case-sensitive)

items.label: Default attribute merge from multiple sources
items.helpKey: Override the default merge strategy for this specific attribute. Choose 'Source name' to always prefer the value from a specific source

items.label: Source name
items.helpKey: Name of the source whose value should be used for this attribute when available. You can also use $originSource to dynamically use the current origin source name.

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Define dynamic computed attributes. Apache Velocity; optional per-definition refresh. Post-template options: case, character normalization, spaces, trim, max length.

Context:
  • Mapped attributes as $name
  • $identity
  • $accounts — ordered by configured sources, then insertion order within each source; non-configured sources are appended
  • $account — the origin snapshot (managed match, or identity-backed row when the origin is Identities). $account may differ from $accounts[0] because $accounts follows the configured source order, not the origin
  • $previous

Snapshot shape:
  • Each $accounts[] entry (and the per-source list in $sources) includes the source account attributes plus:
    • source.id / source.name
    • schema.id (native identity) / schema.name (display name)
  • Identity-backed rows use source.name = "Identities" with no source.id

Sources map:
  • $sources is a Map keyed by source name — access values with dot access, e.g. $sources.SourceName

Order:
  • Top to bottom; each result is available to the next

Helpers:
  • $Math
  • $Datefns — format, parse, parseISO, getYear, addDays/Months/Years, subDays/Months/Years, isBefore, isAfter, isEqual, differenceInDays, startOfDay, endOfDay, now, isValid
  • $Normalize — date, phone, name, fullName, ssn, address; $Normalize.address(address, country?) accepts an optional country code ("US", "GB", or "UK" alias) and normalizes a full state/region name to its ISO code (e.g. "California" → "CA", "Greater London" → "LND"); defaults to "US" and falls back to the trimmed original for unsupported country codes
  • $AddressParse — getCityState, getCityStateCode, parse, getStateName, getStateCode; $AddressParse.getStateName(code, country) returns the full state/region name (or empty string for unknown codes); $AddressParse.getStateCode(name, country) returns the ISO code (case-insensitive; empty string for unknown names); supported countries are "US", "GB", and "UK" (alias for GB); getCityState and getCityStateCode are deprecated due to ambiguous city-only lookups
  • $JSON — stringify / parse ( parse returns undefined for null/non-string/empty/invalid input; stringify returns empty string on failure)

items.label: Normal Attribute Definitions
items.helpKey: Define attributes whose values are defined from templates using mapped account data

items.label: Attribute Name
items.helpKey: Name for this defined attribute on the Fusion account

items.label: Apache Velocity expression
items.helpKey: Velocity template that defines the attribute value. Reference any mapped attribute by name (e.g. $firstname, $lastname, $email). $account is the origin snapshot (managed match, or identity-backed row when the origin is Identities). $accounts[0] is the first snapshot in the ordered list and may differ from $account because $accounts follows the configured source order, not the origin. Managed account snapshots in $accounts / $sources / $account include source (id, name) and schema (id = native identity, name = display); identity-backed $account rows use source.name = Identities (no source.id). Available helpers: $String, $Math, $Datefns, $Normalize, $AddressParse, $JSON (see the section help for the full method list). Example: #set($i=$firstname.substring(0, 1))$i$lastname produces 'jsmith' from 'John Smith'

items.label: Static
items.helpKey: When enabled, the attribute is evaluated only when it has no value. Existing values are never recalculated unless the account is fully reset. This option overrides Refresh on each aggregation if both are enabled.

items.label: Refresh on each aggregation?
items.helpKey: When enabled, the value is recalculated on every aggregation run. When disabled, it is only recalculated when underlying source data changes. If Static is also enabled, Static takes precedence.

items.label: Case selection
items.helpKey: Convert the defined value to a specific letter case

items.label: Normalize special characters?
items.helpKey: Replace accented and special characters with their plain equivalents (e.g. e instead of e with acute)

items.label: Remove spaces?
items.helpKey: Remove all spaces from the defined value

items.label: Trim leading and trailing spaces?
items.helpKey: Remove extra spaces at the beginning and end of the defined value

items.label: Maximum length
items.helpKey: Limit the defined value to this many characters. Leave empty for no limit

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Define persistent unique attributes (e.g. identifiers). Values stay until account reset (e.g. disable/re-enable). Runs after normal definitions on refresh — same Velocity context plus outputs from normal definitions that run first; list order applies within unique definitions too.

Unique variables: $counter — collision mode renders the empty string on the first try and a padded suffix on subsequent attempts (padding per Minimum counter digits), retries capped by Maximum attempts; auto-appended if missing and no $UUID — but the auto-append is skipped when the expression contains Velocity directives (#if, #set, #else, #end, etc.) because appending after #end would break parsing; in that case include $counter explicitly. $UUID: a fresh v4 is generated per attempt when the expression references it. $isUnique(value): a helper injected into unique expressions that returns true when the value (after applying the same case / trim / spaces / normalize / maxLength transforms the definition would apply) is not already registered as in use — useful for choosing between candidate formats before the connector falls back to automatic $counter disambiguation.

Use incremental counter?: when on, the counter is persistent (survives across aggregations) and always increments; the first number comes from Counter start value (default 1). When off (default), the connector uses collision-based disambiguation described above.

Sub-modes of Unique: include $UUID in the expression for UUID generation (the expression is required); toggle Use incremental counter? for sequential IDs.

Helpers: $Normalize (date, phone, name, fullName, ssn, address) — $Normalize.date(date, ambiguousPriority?) accepts an optional priority string like "MM-dd-yyyy,dd-MM-yyyy" for ambiguous dates; $Normalize.phone(phone, defaultCountry?) accepts an optional default country code (e.g. "GB") used when the input lacks an international prefix. $AddressParse (getCityState, getCityStateCode, parse, getStateName, getStateCode). getStateName(code, country) returns the full state/region name (or empty string for unknown codes); getStateCode(name, country) returns the ISO code (case-insensitive; empty string for unknown names). Supported countries are "US", "GB", and "UK" (alias for GB). getCityState and getCityStateCode are deprecated due to ambiguous city-only lookups. Bad inputs render empty. $Math / $Datefns / $JSON (stringify, parse) — see Normal Attribute Definitions.

Reuse: existing values are reused unless this run refreshes the account, the account resets, or a unique value is empty (retry).

items.label: Maximum attempts for unique definition
items.helpKey: Maximum number of tries to find a value that is not already taken. Increase if you have a very large number of existing accounts.

items.label: Unique Attribute Definitions
items.helpKey: Define attributes that must have a unique value across all accounts, such as usernames or employee IDs

items.label: Attribute Name
items.helpKey: Name for this unique attribute on the Fusion account

items.label: Apache Velocity expression
items.helpKey: Velocity template that defines the unique value (required). Use $counter for an automatic number suffix (e.g. jsmith1, jsmith2) — in collision mode $counter renders empty on the first try and as a zero-padded suffix on subsequent attempts (see Minimum counter digits); include $counter explicitly when your expression uses Velocity directives (#if, #set, #end) because the auto-append is skipped in that case. Use $UUID for a fresh v4 random unique ID (include $UUID in the expression for UUID generation). Use $isUnique(value) inside the expression to test whether a candidate value (after this definition's output transforms) is currently free — pick between candidate formats before falling back to $counter. Managed snapshots expose source (id, name) and schema (id, name) on $account / $accounts. Example: #set($i=$firstname.substring(0, 1))$i$lastname$counter

items.label: Minimum counter digits ($counter)
items.helpKey: Minimum number of digits for the counter, padded with leading zeros. For example, 3 digits produces 001, 002, etc.

items.label: Use incremental counter?
items.helpKey: Always assign the next number in sequence instead of only adding a number when there is a conflict. Useful for defining sequential IDs like employee numbers

items.label: Counter start value
items.helpKey: The first number the counter will use. For example, set to 1000 to start numbering from 1000

items.label: Case selection
items.helpKey: Convert the defined value to a specific letter case

items.label: Normalize special characters?
items.helpKey: Replace accented and special characters with their plain equivalents (e.g. e instead of e with acute)

items.label: Remove spaces?
items.helpKey: Remove all spaces from the defined value

items.label: Trim leading and trailing spaces?
items.helpKey: Remove extra spaces at the beginning and end of the defined value

items.label: Maximum length
items.helpKey: Limit the defined value to this many characters. Leave empty for no limit

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Configure similarity-based match detection.

Evaluate matches using Fusion attribute matches to calculate a Combined match score.
  • Algorithms: Text, phonetic, and intelligent gap comparisons.
  • Thresholds & weights: Set minimum scores for individual rules and the overall match. Pass thresholds double as blend weights.
  • Auto-assignment: Optionally bypass manual review and automatically assign the managed account to a matched identity if the combined score meets or exceeds your defined automatic assignment threshold.

items.label: Manual review match score [0-100]
items.helpKey: Minimum weighted combined similarity (0-100) required for a potential match. Mandatory rules must still meet their own minimums.

items.label: Enable automatic assignment
items.helpKey: When enabled, assign the managed account to the matched identity without a review form if the combined score meets or exceeds the automatic assignment match score. Merge and correlation behave like a link-to-existing review, but the fusion account receives the Auto status entitlement only (not Authorized).

items.label: Automatic assignment match score [0-100]
items.helpKey: Matches with a combined score equal to or higher than this threshold will be automatically assigned. Must be greater than the manual review score. If this condition is not met, the connector will fail to initialize with a configuration error.

items.label: Attribute
items.helpKey: The identity attribute to compare when looking for matches (e.g. firstname, lastname, email)

items.label: Matching algorithm
items.helpKey: Algorithm used to compare values. 'Enhanced Name Matcher' excels at strict formatting and accents. 'Jaro-Winkler' is highly tolerant of typographical errors. 'LIG3' balances gaps, missing fragments, and character variations. 'Dice' is forgiving of total word reordering. 'Double Metaphone' captures English phonetic similarity. 'Binary' returns 100 for identical strings and 0 for any difference (case- and whitespace-sensitive). 'Custom Algorithm (Velocity)' runs your Velocity template once per comparison; it must output a numeric score from 0 to 100

options.label: Enhanced Name Matcher
options.docLinkLabel: Strict matching that handles accents and normalization

options.label: Jaro-Winkler
options.docLinkLabel: Mechanical string comparison tolerant of typos

options.label: LIG3
options.docLinkLabel: Advanced hybrid handling missing gaps and character variations

options.label: Dice
options.docLinkLabel: N-gram model highly tolerant of word reordering

options.label: Double Metaphone
options.docLinkLabel: Evaluates strings based on their English pronunciation

items.label: Custom match score (Velocity)
items.helpKey: Apache Velocity template evaluated for each account/identity pair. Context: $accountValue (managed account attribute), $candidateValue (fusion identity attribute), $attribute (this rule's attribute name). Output must be a number from 0 to 100 (similarity score). Same Velocity helpers as attribute definitions ($Math, $Normalize, etc.). Keep expressions efficient; this runs in the hot matching loop.

items.label: Similarity threshold & weight [0-100]
items.helpKey: One setting, two roles: (1) minimum similarity (0-100) the rule must meet to pass, and (2) blend weight in the combined score—higher means stricter and more influence. Use 0 only for minimal weight; it is treated as weight 1 in the blend.

items.label: Mandatory match
items.helpKey: When enabled, this rule must meet its minimum similarity for a potential match. Mandatory rules are always evaluated even when a value is missing (Skip match if missing does not apply), so absent data can fail the rule. Passing mandatory rules contribute to the weighted combined score like other rules.

items.label: Skip match if missing
items.helpKey: When enabled (default), this rule is skipped if either value is missing (null, undefined, or empty after trimming). When disabled, missing values are still compared and count toward the result.

items.label: Skip match if threshold not met
items.helpKey: When enabled, this rule is excluded from the weighted combined match score if its computed similarity is below its minimum similarity (Similarity threshold & weight). Skipped rules contribute zero weight and zero raw score, so the combined score is calculated from the remaining rules. Mandatory rules are always evaluated regardless of this toggle; a below-threshold mandatory rule still fails the candidate. Default: disabled.

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Configure manual review for potential matches.

Define Form attributes to display to reviewers and set candidate limits. Assign global reviewers to act as fail-safes and optionally email them processing reports after aggregation runs.

items.label: List of Fusion account attributes to include in form
items.helpKey: Account attributes displayed on the review form to help reviewers compare potential matches. For example: name, email, department

items.label: Maximum candidates per review form
items.helpKey: Maximum number of potential identity matches shown on each manual review form. If more identities qualify, only the highest-scoring candidates are included (combined match score, then stable tie-break). Valid range: 1–15.

items.label: Manual review expiration days
items.helpKey: Number of days a reviewer has to respond before the review form expires.

items.label: Owners are global reviewers?
items.helpKey: Always add the source owner and any member of the source's assigned governance group as reviewers on every review form, ensuring someone is always assigned to review potential matches

items.label: Send report to owner on aggregation?
items.helpKey: Send a summary report to the source owner after each run, including potential matches, processing outcomes, and source-type breakdown metrics

items.label: Enable localized user communications?
items.helpKey: Translate emails, reports, and Fusion reviews to the recipient's preferred language. This depends on an identity language attribute.

items.label: Default Language
items.helpKey: The default language to use when the recipient's language cannot be determined.

items.label: Identity Language Attribute
items.helpKey: Identity attribute containing the user's preferred language. Recognizes common language formats (e.g. 'en', 'eng', 'english', 'en-US').

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Advanced options for troubleshooting and performance tuning.

Use these settings to safely recover from configuration changes (e.g. rebuilding accounts or forcing attribute recalculation), manage memory consumption during match detection by adjusting batch sizes, and configure external logging for centralized monitoring.

items.label: Reset accounts?
items.helpKey: Rebuild all Fusion accounts from scratch on the next run. Use with caution in production and remember to turn this off after it completes

items.label: Force attribute refresh on next aggregation?
items.helpKey: On the next aggregation run only, recalculate all computed Normal-type attributes even if no changes were detected. After that run completes, this option is automatically turned off. This may increase processing time but ensures values stay up to date when you need a one-time refresh

items.label: Enable concurrency check?
items.helpKey: Safeguard against data conflicts if multiple aggregations overlap. Recommended to keep enabled

items.label: Enable external logging?
items.helpKey: Stream connector execution logs directly to external monitoring services like Splunk or Datadog for centralized troubleshooting

items.label: External logging URL
items.helpKey: The URL where logs should be sent (e.g. your Splunk or logging service endpoint)

items.label: External logging level
items.helpKey: Choose the detail level for external logs. 'Error' sends only critical issues. 'Debug' sends everything, which is useful for troubleshooting but produces more data

items.label: Managed accounts batch size
items.helpKey: Number of uncorrelated managed accounts processed in each match detection batch. Lower values reduce peak memory usage and may improve stability in constrained environments; higher values can improve throughput at the cost of more memory. Typical tuning range: 25-100.

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Fine-tune API limits and execution resilience.

Adjust these parameters to prevent the connector from being rate-limited by Identity Security Cloud, ensure long-running operations complete without timing out, and optimize the throughput by adjusting request concurrency and batching sizes.

items.label: Provisioning timeout (seconds)
items.helpKey: Maximum time (in seconds) to wait for a provisioning operation to complete. Increase this if you experience timeouts with large batches.

items.label: Maximum concurrent requests
items.helpKey: How many requests can run at the same time. Lower values are safer for rate-limited APIs.

items.label: Requests per second
items.helpKey: Maximum number of requests sent per second. Reduce this if you are getting rate-limit errors.

items.label: API request retries
items.helpKey: How many times to retry a failed request before giving up.

items.label: Processing wait time (seconds)
items.helpKey: How often (in seconds) to send a progress signal during long operations to prevent timeouts.

items.label: Enable priority processing?
items.helpKey: Process critical operations (like saving data) before less urgent ones (like logging). Recommended for best performance

items.sectionHelpMessage:
Delegate processing to your own infrastructure.

Configure the connector to route all processing through a self-hosted proxy server, which allows you to execute operations outside of the cloud environment while maintaining secure authentication.

items.label: Enable proxy mode?
items.helpKey: Offload processing workload to your own infrastructure by routing operations through a dedicated server, which is useful for highly restricted or specialized environments

items.label: Proxy URL
items.helpKey: The URL of your proxy server that will handle connector operations

items.label: Proxy password
items.helpKey: A shared secret used to authenticate with your proxy server. This must match the password configured on the proxy

attributes.name: missing-accounts
attributes.description: Missing managed account keys (sourceId::nativeIdentity; legacy raw IDs supported)

attributes.name: mainAccount
attributes.description: Managed account ID evaluated first when present

attributes.name: originSource
